MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the next number in the pattern 2, 6, 18, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 36
   B. 24
   C. 20
   D. 54

2. Work out 7,305 + 2,489. (1 mark)
   A. 9,784
   B. 9,794
   C. 9,694
   D. 9,804

3. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 3 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 12. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 4:00
   B. 12:15
   C. 3:12
   D. 3:00

4. A triangle has sides of 10 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 38 cm
   B. 39 cm
   C. 37 cm
   D. 44 cm

5. How long is a lesson that starts at 7:40 a.m. and ends at 9:10 a.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 30 min
   B. 1 h 30 min
   C. 1 h 40 min
   D. 1 h 15 min

6. Which shape is a cuboid? (1 mark)
   A. A matchbox
   B. A plate
   C. A football
   D. A coin

7. A customer pays with Ksh 500 for goods that cost Ksh 235. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 735
   B. Ksh 365
   C. Ksh 255
   D. Ksh 265

8. If p = 5, what is the value of 4p + 3? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 23
   C. 12
   D. 43

9. One layer of a cuboid has 9 blocks and there are 6 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 54 blocks
   B. 63 blocks
   C. 48 blocks
   D. 15 blocks

10. Change 7 m 60 cm to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 130 cm
   B. 7,600 cm
   C. 760 cm
   D. 67 cm

11. In 5,432 − 2,718, the ones digit 2 is smaller than 8. From which digit do we borrow? (1 mark)
   A. We swap the 2 and the 8
   B. The hundreds digit 4, which becomes 3
   C. The thousands digit 5, which becomes 4
   D. The tens digit 3, which becomes 2

12. A hundred square has 48 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 0.48
   B. 4.8
   C. 0.048
   D. 48

13. The table shows the favourite sports of 10 pupils: football 5, netball 3, athletics 1, swimming 1. Which one has the greatest number? (1 mark)
   A. swimming
   B. athletics
   C. football
   D. netball

14. Which Roman numeral stands for 9? (1 mark)
   A. VX
   B. IX
   C. IIII
   D. VIIII

15. Musa covers a book cover with 12 rows of 9 squares. Which sum gives the number of squares? (1 mark)
   A. 12 − 9
   B. 12 ÷ 9
   C. 12 + 9
   D. 12 × 9

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Ten pupils chose their favourite drink: 4 chose juice, 3 chose milk, 2 chose water and 1 chose tea. Write two facts that you can read from this data. (2 marks)

17. Find and name three objects in the classroom that show a rectangle, a circle and a triangle. (3 marks)

18. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. Draw it roughly, label the sides and find its perimeter. (3 marks)

19. List four materials you could use to collect and record data about the types of vehicles that pass the school gate. (4 marks)

20. A dial scale has big marks for each kilogram and three small marks between them. What mass does the first small mark after 3 kg show? Explain. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 54
   The rule is multiply by 3. 18 × 3 = 54.

2. B — 9,794
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 7,305 + 2,489 = 9,794.

3. D — 3:00
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 12 shows 12 × 5 = 0 minutes, so the time is 3:00.

4. C — 37 cm
   Add all three sides: 10 + 12 + 15 = 37 cm.

5. B — 1 h 30 min
   Count on from 7:40 a.m. to 9:10 a.m.. The total is 1 h 30 min.

6. A — A matchbox
   A matchbox has six rectangular faces, so it is a cuboid.

7. D — Ksh 265
   Change = amount paid − cost = 500 − 235 = Ksh 265.

8. B — 23
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 23.

9. A — 54 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 9 × 6 = 54 blocks.

10. C — 760 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 7 × 100 = 700, and 700 + 60 = 760. So the answer is 760 cm.

11. D — The tens digit 3, which becomes 2
   Borrow one ten from the tens column. The 3 becomes 2 and the ones digit 2 becomes 12.

12. A — 0.48
   48 out of 100 squares is 48/100 = 0.48.

13. C — football
   The biggest number is 5, which belongs to football.

14. B — IX
   9 is written IX. I before X is 10 − 1.

15. D — 12 × 9
   Squares = rows × columns = 12 × 9 = 108.

SECTION B
----
16. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: juice is the most popular with 4 pupils; only 1 pupil chose tea; 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 pupils were asked.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fact based on the numbers.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example a blackboard (rectangle), a clock face (circle) and a set square (triangle).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct object matched to a shape.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Perimeter = 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a labelled rectangle, 1 mark for adding all four sides, 1 mark for 26 cm.

19. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: a pencil, an exercise book or paper, a ruler for drawing a table, a clipboard or hard book, a watch or clock.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible material.

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/4 kg. The three small marks divide each kilogram into four equal parts of 1/4 kg.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 3 1/4 kg, 1 mark for four equal parts, 1 mark for 1/4 kg each.
